Definition: from a primary στίζω (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service:--mark.
BiblicalUsage: The mark is the brand cut into the flesh, and Paul says, from henceforth let no man trouble me, for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus. The scars of his beatings are the brand of his Master.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the marks are Paul's credentials: not letters of commendation, but scars that say whose he is.
